item.title: Gambling bills struggle to remain alive amid Hawaii’s prohibition on wagering
item.description: A bill that would allow cruise ship gambling — even while ships are docked in Hawaii ports — stalled in a House committee Wednesday while another bill that would allow sports betting squeaked through as the state Legislature continues to debate whether to end Hawaii’s prohibition on gambling.

item.title: State Board of Education adopts new policy on student cellphone use; implementation begins next school year
item.description: Keiki, get ready to put your cellphones away.

item.title: Portion of shoreline closed after sewage spill at Papaikou Treatment Plant
item.description: A sewage spill at the Papaikou Treatment Plant has resulted in a shoreline closure.

item.title: Trump administration to end surge of immigration agents in Minnesota
item.description: ST. PAUL, Minn. — The Trump administration said Thursday that it was ending its deployment of immigration agents to Minnesota, unwinding an aggressive operation that has stretched for more than two months despite loud opposition from residents and local officials.

item.title: Runnin’ with Rani: Youth track and field meet returns to Waverider Stadium
item.description: KAILUA-KONA — Kealakehe High School’s Waverider Stadium filled early on Saturday as young athletes from West and East Hawaii took to the blue track for the Hawaii County Department of Parks & Recreation’s annual Youth Track and Field Meet.

item.title: Wahine Marlin Tournament donates $10k to charity
item.description: KAILUA-KONA — One of the most exciting big-game fishing tournaments on the island made its recent return to West Hawaii this past summer, and is here to stay for the future.

item.title: US judge blocks Pentagon’s effort to punish Senator Mark Kelly
item.description: A U.S. judge blocked the Pentagon on Thursday from reducing Senator Mark Kelly’s retired military rank and pension pay as punishment after he urged troops to reject unlawful orders. The preliminary ruling by U.S. District Judge Richard Leon in Washington is the latest setback in court for President Donald Trump’s historic campaign of vengeance against his perceived political enemies, which has drawn pushback from judges across the ideological spectrum.

item.title: House votes to cancel Trump’s Canada tariffs
item.description: WASHINGTON — The House voted Wednesday to rescind tariffs that President Donald Trump imposed on Canada last year, delivering a largely symbolic but politically consequential rebuke that Republicans had fought for a year to prevent.

item.title: Green cancels D.C. trip to avoid having Sylvia Luke fill in as governor
item.description: Gov. Josh Green has canceled his upcoming plans to travel to Washington, D.C., for the annual National Governors Association’s Winter Meeting to avoid having Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke fill in for him as acting governor after she acknowledged Monday that she may be the “influential state legislator” who is being investigated for allegedly accepted $35,000 in a bag in 2022.
